cases.label: Quantity truncates toward zero at the int limits and on halves: 2147483647.999, -2147483648.999, 0.500, -0.500, 1.500, -1.505, 0.005; rows inserted in descending id order with gaps
cases.reasoning: CAST(decimal(18,3) AS int) truncates in T-SQL. The conversion uses TRUNC then a cast; a plain ::integer cast rounds half away from zero (0.5 -> 1, -0.5 -> -1) and would overflow on 2147483647.999. Ids 21, 13, 8, 5, 3, 2, 1 are inserted in that order, so a result relying on insertion order instead of ORDER BY would come back reversed. All rows share StockItemID 1.

top-ties.detail: two rows of Warehouse.StockItemTransactions share StockItemID = 1

cases.label: window at the extremes of datetime2: @LastCutoff 0001-01-01 00:00:00, @NewCutoff 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999; rows at both instants and 1 µs inside
cases.reasoning: A row edited exactly at 0001-01-01 is excluded (> is strict); 1 µs later is included; 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999 equals @NewCutoff and is included (<=). TransactionOccurredWhen 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999 must give Date Key 9999-12-31 (truncation, not rounding into year 10000) and 1753-01-01 must stay 1753-01-01.

cases.label: empty window: @LastCutoff equal to @NewCutoff; rows at that instant and 1 µs either side are all excluded
cases.reasoning: > @LastCutoff AND <= @NewCutoff with equal cutoffs can never hold. A conversion that used BETWEEN or >= on the lower bound would return the row edited at exactly 12:00:00.

cases.label: inverted window: @LastCutoff after @NewCutoff returns nothing, even for rows between them
cases.reasoning: With @LastCutoff = 13:00 and @NewCutoff = 11:00 both predicates are never true together. A conversion that normalised the window (LEAST/GREATEST) or swapped the parameters would return the rows at 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00.

cases.label: day rollover in the microsecond digits: cutoffs at 23:59:59.999999; Date Key of 23:59:59.999999 stays on that day; Quantity 0.999 and -0.995 truncate to 0
cases.reasoning: @LastCutoff 2020-06-14 23:59:59.999999 excludes a row at that instant and includes the next midnight; @NewCutoff 2020-06-15 23:59:59.999999 includes a row at that instant and excludes the next midnight. The included rows occurred at 23:59:59.999999, whose CAST to date keeps the day. -0.995 and 0.999 truncate to 0 (a rounding cast would give -1 and 1).
